newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech central bank move to boost markets-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Czech central bank move to boost markets-analysts.

text.p: A reduction by the Czech central bank in its minimum reserve requirements for banks fell short of an expected interest rate cut, but should still lift bond and money markets, analysts said on Friday.

The Czech National Bank (CNB) on Thursday cut the level of compulsory deposits which banks must hold with the central bank to 9.5 from 11.5 percent, effective May 8. But it failed to trim offical interest rates.
Bond and money markets posted gains on Friday, with some analysts predicting the move could add up to 20 billion crowns ($670 million) in extra liquidity to those sectors.

"(This) will be placed primarily in the money and bond markets. Short-term yields have already begun to decline and the long-end of the market should follow," said Jack Schrantz of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment in Prague.
Demand was also underpinned by investors asset-swapping.
"There's an arbitrage opportunity developing between taking fixed income items in the Czech Republic and swapping them out into hard currency," said Matt Starr at Creditanstalt in Prague.

The CNB raised the minimum reserve requirement and put up interest rates last year as part of measures aimed at tackling stubbornly high inflation by slowing money supply growth. But it has come under heavy political pressure lately to ease off as the economy has slowed down.

Dealers said that while there was no rate cut on Thursday, the central bank might still act next week, in tandem with the government, which will announce a series of measures to spur the economy on April 16.
"The market is building in a possible interest rate cut, which could come...as part of measures the government is preparing to help the trade deficit," said one London trader.

Senior government officials have blamed the central bank's tight monetary policy for the economic slowdown and many foreign exchange dealers are sure the CNB will cut rates soon. The official discount rate is 10.50 percent.
The Czech economy has enjoyed several years of demand-led growth, but cracks have begun to appear with industrial output failing to keep pace with wages, and even contracting recently.
Czech equities, slow to react to most market news, edged up at the Prague Stock Exchange's daily price fixing, with banking shares leading the way.
"The news of a lowering of the reserve requirement could spark a rally in banking stocks, which would be a good time to take profits," said Schrantz.

Radek Vavra, head of Citicorp Securities in Prague, said he too expected banking stocks to rise, though the effects may be delayed. "If there's going to be an impact, it'll be long-term -- six months down the road."

The crown held steady most of the day after an early dip against its dollar/mark basket. The CNB fixed the crown at 29.790 to the dollar and at 17.315 to the mark versus 29.621 and 17.262 on Thursday. ($ = 29.79 Czech Crowns)
